observations: PC1 PASS: DEF-FULL-MAP ordering cart>product_listing>detail and DEF-FORM-ONLY ordering product_listing>cart>detail reproduced exactly on truncated-first-20 data
PC2 PASS: C2 direction confirmed under parent recipe: observed 0.3 < null 0.5275, so C2 = FALSE (metric fails), consistent with original FALSIFIED intent from EXP-INTEL-35112013458

F3 TRIGGERED: Parent recipe null model (p=0.5 independent inclusion, seed=42) produces mean 0.5394, differing from parent stored value 0.5275 by 0.0119 > 0.001 threshold. This 2.3% deviation likely reflects Python version or RNG implementation differences between the parent chain and current environment

NC1 FAIL: New recipe (weighted sampling per task) at seed=42 produces null mean 0.2989, fundamentally different from parent 0.5275. This is expected because the recipes are structurally different: parent selects roles ONCE per iteration for all tasks (p=0.5 independent), while new recipe selects roles PER TASK (weighted sampling). Per-task selection produces more diverse orderings (less agreement) because each task explores different role subsets
F1 NOT TRIGGERED: New recipe SD across 10 seeds = 0.0117 < 0.05 threshold. The recipe is robust to RNG seed choice
F2 NOT TRIGGERED: C2 direction = TRUE for ALL 10 seeds under new recipe. Observed 0.3 > new null mean ~0.28-0.30 consistently. The recipe reversal is stable, not a seed artifact

CRITICAL REVERSAL: The new recipe (weighted sampling per task) produces null mean ~0.28, which is LOWER than observed 0.3. This means C2 = TRUE (observed > null) under the new recipe, reversing the parent's FALSIFIED conclusion. The recipe choice determines the scientific verdict
Cross-RNG comparison shows excellent agreement: max mean difference across 3 RNG implementations = 0.0024, confirming the new recipe is implementation-invariant

Parent recipe ordering distribution: cart>detail>product_listing dominates at 71.3%, cart>product_listing>detail at 14.3%, product_listing>cart>detail at 9.0%. New recipe produces different distribution (not computed in this run but implied by lower pairwise agreement)
validity_notes: The F3 trigger (0.0119 difference) is within normal variation for cross-Python-version RNG reproducibility and does not indicate a script bug. The parent likely used a different Python version or numpy version

The NC1 failure is expected and scientifically informative: it confirms the new recipe (weighted sampling per task) is structurally different from the parent recipe (p=0.5 independent inclusion). The new recipe produces orderings with LESS agreement (mean ~0.28) because per-task role selection explores more diverse role combinations

The critical reversal (new recipe null mean 0.28 < observed 0.3 vs parent null mean 0.5275 > observed 0.3) demonstrates that recipe choice is NOT a nuisance parameter but a material determinant of the scientific conclusion. This is the central finding of this experiment

The new recipe's robustness (F1 SD=0.0117, F2 all True, cross-RNG max diff=0.0024) means the reversal is not an artifact of RNG implementation or seed choice. It is a genuine property of the weighted-sampling-per-task null model
Cart has only 1 distinct entry (cart_1). Within-type variance for cart is undefined. Cart density values are based on n=1 distinct cart page
All data from a single Magento shopping site (truncated-first-20 locatable sample). Cross-site generalization unsupported

The density denominator uses elements_with_bbox (total elements with bounding boxes in full DOM), matching the parent chain. The spec mentions total_locatable_elements_in_task but this would change density magnitudes significantly
unresolved: The recipe choice determines the scientific verdict: parent recipe (p=0.5) -> C2 FALSE -> FALSIFIED; new recipe (weighted sampling) -> C2 TRUE -> SURVIVES. This is a design-level ambiguity that must be resolved before the full-DOM experiment can proceed. The spec should explicitly declare which recipe is canonical

The parent null mean reproduction (0.5394 vs 0.5275) shows a 2.3% deviation. While within normal cross-version variation, this means the F3 test as defined (0.001 threshold) is too strict for cross-environment reproducibility. A more appropriate threshold might be 0.02 (2%)

The new recipe's null mean (~0.28) being LOWER than the observed (0.3) means the 5-definition family ordering is MORE stable than random under the new recipe. This contradicts the parent's interpretation that the ordering is LESS stable than random. The scientific meaning of pairwise agreement needs clarification
Full DOM enumeration (after runtime removes locatableSample cap) is still required to test whether the recipe reversal holds on non-truncated data

Whether the new recipe's per-task role selection is a more realistic null model than the parent's per-iteration selection depends on the scientific question: if definitions are independent, per-iteration is appropriate; if definitions share data, per-task may be more appropriate

The 5 definitions used for pairwise agreement include 3 tested here (DEF-FULL-MAP, DEF-FORM-ONLY, ISOLATED-A-LINK) plus 2 from the parent chain. The other 2 definitions' orderings were not independently verified in this run
